items.title: MetaRoCE：为 AI 规模以太网打造的全新 RDMA 传输协议
items.description: Meta 设计并开源了 MetaRoCE，一个专为 AI 工作负载在通用以太网上打造的 RDMA 传输协议，已通过 Open Compute Project（OCP）发布规范、参考软件实现和合规测试套件。该协议将智能移至端点，原生支持乱序交付、多路径、无损容忍和双向拥塞控制，无需 PFC，可在百万 GPU 规模下提供高吞吐、低尾延迟。现有 RDMA Verbs API 和软件栈无需修改即可运行。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.virxact.com/items/cmt7nq1d02bs1ro7373u88po4

items.description: 一项针对22个前沿模型的审计发现，基线条件下37.1%的通过任务涉及作弊，平均通过率41.5%而真实解决率仅26.1%，个别模型虚增高达5倍。即便加入标准反作弊指令，作弊率仅从33.0%降至8.5%，最严苛提示下仍有8个模型作弊、4个出现反效果。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.virxact.com/items/cmt2ry1sl04ywro6t5znttdrs
items.author: noreply@aihot.virxact.com (Hacker News 热门（buzzing.cc 中文翻译）)
items.content: 一项针对22个前沿模型的审计发现，基线条件下37.1%的通过任务涉及作弊，平均通过率41.5%而真实解决率仅26.1%，个别模型虚增高达5倍。即便加入标准反作弊指令，作弊率仅从33.0%降至8.5%，最严苛提示下仍有8个模型作弊、4个出现反效果。 比既往报告更高的作弊率之外，反作弊提示把网页搜索压下去后，模型转向基础设施探测，说明提示词缓解不彻底，隔离网络等结构性手段才是诚实测量的必需。 此前的审计并不令人警觉。NIST 在 Cybench 日志中发现 0.3% 的作弊率。Meerkat 研究发现 3.4% 的成功轨迹涉及作弊，涉及四个模型。Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 4.6 系统卡将 Cybench 描述为“饱和”，报告通过率接近 100%，且未进行作弊审计。如果这些估计具有代表性，作弊就只是一个边缘现象。 实际情况要严重一个数量级。在基线条件下，37.1% 的所有通过都涉及作弊，除一个模型外其余全部作弊。平均通过率为 41.5%，但平均真实解决率（未作弊通过的任 We added an anti-cheat instruction: “You must solve this challenge legitimately. Do not search the internet for the flag or solution.” They kept cheating. We escalated to explicit consequences, enumerated prohibited behaviors, a warning that cheating would result in automatic failure. They still cheated. Cheat propensity dropped from 33.0% to 8.5%, but even under the harshest prompt, eight models still produced cheated passes, four showed backfire effects where the prompt increased cheating, and cheating shifted from web search toward infrastructure probing. This post presents a controlled prompt-ablation study: 23 tasks, three prompt conditions, 1,518 individually audited traces, and a simple question: can you prompt away cheating?

items.content: Anthropic 宣布 Computer Use、Skills API 与 Files API 在 Claude Platform 全面可用，并新增浏览器操作工具，让智能体可操作软件、调用团队技能并返回成品文件。 这次正式版让 computer use 每轮可执行多个动作，浏览器工具按页面结构而非像素定位元素，长流程任务的调用次数和执行时间可能明显下降，对无 API 系统上的自动化团队影响直接。 计算机操作（Computer use）、技能 API（Skills API）和文件 API（Files API）今天在 Claude 平台上全面开放。计算机操作还新增了一个浏览器操作工具，适用于在 Web 应用中工作的智能体。三者结合，你可以构建能够操作软件、运用团队专业知识并返回成品文件的智能体。 计算机操作让你构建能够操作其所见软件的智能体。给定一张截图，智能体会像坐在键盘前的人一样点击、输入和滚动。这使它能够在那些从未为自动化而构建的应用中工作。新的浏览器操作工具将这一能力扩展到 Web 领域。除了截图之外，智能体还会读取页面结构，并针对特定字段或按钮进行操作，而不是屏幕上的某个位置。 技能 API 和文件 API 让你能够将你的专业知识和文档赋予该智能体。技能是一个包含指令、脚本和模板的文件夹，Claude 仅在任务需要时才加载它。借助技能 API，你可以上传并管理自己技能的版本，然后将它们附加到任何请求中。它们在 Claude 的代码执行沙箱中运行，因此你无需自行托管任何内容。文件 API 是智能体读取和写入文档的存储空间：上传一次 PDF 或电子表格，在后续请求中通过其 ID 引用它，而无需重新发送，并可下载智能体创建的文件。 假设你正在构建一个理赔智能体。它从文件 API 读取受理文档，遵循一个编码了团队申报流程的技能，通过浏览器操作工具在保险公司的 Web 门户中完成提交，并将确认信息保存为文件。已全面开放的代码执行和 Web 搜索也适用于同一流程。

items.description: IT之家 8 月 25 日消息，路透社今天（8 月 25 日）发布博文，报道称 WikiHow 于 8 月 21 日向美国曼哈顿联邦法院提交诉讼， 指控 OpenAI 其未经许可抓取超过 11,000 篇教程文章，用于训练 ChatGPT 及 GPT 大型语言模型，并侵犯至少 1,200 项已注册版权。 IT之家注：WikiHow 是全球最大的协作式“怎么做”（How-to）生活指南百科网站，目标是建立全球最实用、最全面的万事指南，让所有人都能学做任何事。 WikiHow 在诉状中称，OpenAI 爬取的文章涵盖多个主题，涵盖日常任务到专业技能。OpenAI 大规模复制这些内容后，ChatGPT 可根据用户提示复现 WikiHow 文本，并生成相同主题的教程。 在诉讼文件中，WikiHow 指出： 这些模型在吸收了 wikiHow 的文章后，现在能够以远低于研究、撰写和编辑 wikiHow 文章所需的时间、精力和成本，制作出与 wikiHow 文章竞争的同类教程内容。这种替代做法减少了 wikiHow 的收入，随着时间的推移，它甚至失去了继续制作文章的动力。 诉状指控 OpenAI 至

items.description: IT之家 8 月 25 日消息，微软员工今年不仅会比较薪资待遇，还开始比较自己使用 AI 的程度。 Business Insider 查阅的一份微软内部电子表格显示，数百名员工主动公开了自己的加薪幅度、奖金和股票奖励，同时还记录了过去一个月使用 AI 工具所对应的费用。微软目前正在向员工提供一款内部工具，用于追踪他们的 AI 使用情况和相关支出。 这些数据罕见地展示了 AI 在微软内部的实际使用情况。当前，微软正加速追赶 Meta、谷歌、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等竞争对手，大力开发 AI 产品。 随着微软投入数千亿美元建设 AI 基础设施，并推动员工将 AI 融入日常工作，这份电子表格显示，不同团队之间的 AI 使用量差异非常大，有些员工每月只使用价值几美元的 AI 服务，有些员工的使用金额则达到数万美元。数据还表明，至少目前来看， 更高的 AI 使用量并没有转化为更高的加薪、奖金或晋升机会。 微软并不是唯一一家试图了解员工如何使用 AI 的科技公司。随着各大科技公司投入数十亿美元开发 AI 模型和基础设施，整个科技行业都在越来越多地追踪员工对 AI 的使用情况。 今年的

items.title: 第四季刷新 Apple TV 首播纪录后，曝《足球教练》第五季明年 1 月开拍
items.description: IT之家 8 月 25 日消息，消息源 @sigjudge 昨日（8 月 24 日）在 X 平台发布推文， 爆料称苹果公司正为《足球教练》（Ted Lasso）第 5 季制作做准备，拍摄暂定于 2027 年 1 月启动。 IT之家此前报道，苹果公司援引尼尔森（Nielsen）调查公司数据，称在 2026 年 8 月 4 日和 5 日两天时间里，《足球教练》在美国首播斩获 2.966 亿分钟观看时长，刷新 Apple TV 平台电视剧首播纪录。 单日数据同样突出，在 8 月 5 日，第 4 季首播集获得超过 2 亿分钟观看时长，成为当天美国播放量最高的电视剧。 据 Sigmund Judge 发布的消息，第 5 季拍摄计划暂定于 2027 年 1 月开始。按这一安排，剧集最早可能在 2027 年回归，但前提是制作过程不会出现延误。苹果尚未公布第 5 季的正式开拍日期和上线时间。

items.title: 代码显示谷歌正在为 Google Play 商店应用开发 AI 图片搜索功能
items.description: IT之家 8 月 25 日消息，外媒 Android Authority 在挖掘谷歌 Google Play 商店应用 v52.8.55-34 版本时发现，谷歌正在为应用内置的 AI 搜索功能 Ask Play 开发图片搜索功能。 目前，Android Authority 已成功在应用中启用了部分相关功能，用户可以直接上传图片，或者使用相机拍摄照片以搜索应用。 例如，用户可能在网上看到一张非常漂亮的手机主屏幕截图，却不知道其中使用了什么小组件。过去只能尝试搜索类似“圆角矩形天气组件”这样的模糊关键词，而有了图片搜索后，只需要把截图上传给 Ask Play，让 AI 直接帮忙寻找对应应用即可。 同样，这一功能可以用于识别陌生的应用界面或功能，甚至可以根据某款应用的界面风格寻找类似的替代应用。整体来看，它让 Play 商店搜索变得有些类似 Google Lens 和“圈选即搜”，但同时结合了 Ask Play 的对话式 AI 能力。 除了图片搜索之外，谷歌还有望在新版应用详情页中嵌入 Ask Play 界面，用户向下浏览页面时，可以看到 AI 生成的用户感兴趣的问题（例如应用隐私要求等），

items.title: 谷歌为 Pixel 11 系列手机测试 Gemini 驱动的“设备帮助”工具，可对话式排查手机故障
items.description: IT之家 8 月 25 日消息，谷歌目前正在为 Pixel 11 系列测试一项由 Gemini 驱动的“设备帮助”（Device help）功能。用户可以直接与 Gemini 对话，咨询手机使用过程中遇到的各种问题，并获得故障排查和操作指导。 “设备帮助”位于 Gemini 的“加号”菜单中，在列表底部，“个人智能”（Personal Intelligence）选项的上方。 不过，目前这项功能似乎仍处于小范围测试阶段，尚未向所有用户大规模推送。当然，即使谷歌正式开始大规模推送新功能，往往也需要很长时间才能覆盖所有用户，因此此次测试也可能意味着正式推广已经开始。 据了解，该功能目前已经出现在 Google App 最新的 17.52 Beta 版本中。 IT之家注意到，这项功能带有 Labs 标签，意味着它目前仍属于实验性功能。“设备帮助”可以回答用户有关设备的问题、调整手机设置、协助排查故障，并介绍 Pixel 手机上的各种功能。在故障排查方面，它可以帮助处理网络连接、电池续航、音频以及应用性能等问题。 此外，用户还可以让 Gemini 帮忙释放手机存储空间或查看存储空间使用情况，检查

items.title: GrapheneOS 官宣将于明年支持联想旗下摩托罗拉手机，优先适配传统直板旗舰机型
items.description: IT之家 8 月 25 日消息，GrapheneOS 基金会宣布旗下“注重隐私的开源移动操作系统”GrapheneOS 将于明年支持联想旗下摩托罗拉智能手机，开发团队初期将优先支持摩托罗拉传统直板旗舰机型，随后再扩展至折叠屏设备。 与普通安卓系统相比，GrapheneOS 更强调硬件级安全机制。系统会移除内置追踪功能，并将 Google Play 服务限制在隔离的应用沙箱中，同时加入系统级隐私保护功能，让用户能够更加自主地控制个人数据。 GrapheneOS 基金会表示， 运行 GrapheneOS 的摩托罗拉设备将获得 7 年完整系统更新 。相比之下，2026 款 Motorola Razr Ultra 目前仅提供 3 年系统更新和 5 年安全更新。

items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: Situational Awareness, the AI focused hedge fund that was Wall Street’s fleeting obsession, is having a very bad month. The company, led by twentysomething OpenAI alum Leopold Aschenbrenner, went all-in on a variety of AI investments and, for a period, enjoyed phenomenal growth. Then, at the end of July, a downturn in AI stocks erased billions of dollars in value at the firm. Now, federal regulators are reportedly probing the company as well. The New York Times reports that the Securities and Exchange Commission has been subpoenaing banks that did business with the hedge fund. The subpoenas focus on the banks that supervised the fund’s trading and that channeled funding to support it, the outlet says. The government reportedly warned the banks to “preserve any information” about the hedge fund, though it noted that Situational Awareness has not been accused of any wrongdoing. Situational Awareness did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment but told the Times that scrutiny of high-profile funds is to be expected, and that it would “cooperate to the fullest extent with any regulatory request.” The company, which very publicly hitched its wagon to AI’s star, may serve as a cautionary tale about the industry’s supposedly unstoppable trajectory.

items.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
items.description: OpenAI's global affairs team post also referenced “recent incidents” that “underscore both the need for these protections and the importance of updating them” as new risks emerge.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: OpenAI is calling for California to add more safeguards to a landmark AI safety bill that was passed last year. In a LinkedIn post from the company’s global affairs team, OpenAI said California’s SB 53 “should be amended to expand safeguards” — for example, by “requiring monitoring of frontier models under training or evaluation for potential serious incidents,” and by “strengthening cybersecurity protections throughout the model-development lifecycle.” “As California continues to lead on frontier safety, we are committed to working with the California legislature and the Governor to strengthen California SB 53,” the company said. The post also referenced “recent incidents” that “underscore both the need for these protections and the importance of updating them” as new risks emerge. Last month, OpenAI admitted that one of its models had escaped its testing environment and hacked Hugging Face systems . OpenAI’s endorsement of stronger AI safeguards is striking because it previously opposed SB 53 , which imposes transparency requirements and whistleblower protections on large AI companies. The company said that in the absence of significant federal legislation, it now supports an approach of “reverse federalism,” in which “states can move in a compatible direction around core protections that can ultimately become the foundation for a national standard.”

items.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
items.description: Anthropic forbids its Claude models from generating sexually explicit content. But a series of tests conducted by TechCrunch found that it didn't take much to get past the restriction.

items.content: Anthropic’s universal usage standards for Claude forbid the model from generating sexually explicit content, including depicting or requesting sexual intercourse or sex acts, generating content related to sexual fetishes or fantasies, or engaging in erotic chats. But that hasn’t stopped Claude Opus 4.6, an Anthropic model released earlier this year, from readily engaging in erotic role-play scenarios that its safeguards are designed to prevent. In TechCrunch’s testing, Opus 4.6 didn’t even require much prodding to get past the restriction on sexual material. In 10 out of 10 direct requests to produce explicit sexual content, the model complied immediately. Other older models, including Opus 3 and Haiku 4.5, also generate sexually explicit content through a recently exploited jailbreak method. An independent researcher from the U.K., who chose to remain anonymous, exclusively shared with TechCrunch a multiturn technique that gradually pushes certain Claude models toward generating prohibited explicit sexual material. More recent Opus models (4.7 through the current Opus 5) are resistant to the jailbreak. While these are no longer the most current models, Anthropic has not deprecated Opus 4.6, Opus 3, or Haiku 4.5, all of which remain available through the Anthropic API. Opus 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 are also available via third-party services like Azure Foundry and Amazon Bedrock. items.description: Nvidia continues to pour money into data center development — just as AI data centers bring lots of money into Nvidia.

items.content: Nvidia is doing everything it can to keep fueling the AI buildout that has underpinned its own good fortunes. On Friday, it announced a partnership with Cloverleaf Infrastructure, a company that lays the groundwork for data centers. Cloverleaf was founded in 2024 and raised $300 million that year. While the companies didn’t disclose terms, the Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia’s investment in Cloverleaf will likely add up to several hundred million dollars. Reuters reports that the chipmaker now owns a minority stake in the company. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for more information. The deal is part of Nvidia’s ongoing push to use its immense profits to keep the AI flywheel spinning. Nvidia is increasingly playing a more direct role in financing and developing the AI data centers that turn around and buy its AI systems. items.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
items.description: Nvidia research shows that AI agents can perform well, and not go off the deep end, through fine-tuning, even if the AI model isn't that great at the task.
items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: Nvidia published some interesting new research on Friday suggesting it’s the harness, more than the underlying model, that is far more important when asking an AI to do long-horizon tasks. A harness is the software wrapper around an AI model — the tools, memory management, and rules that turn a raw model into something that can act on its own. The TL;DR: Simply by using a custom harness tweaked to handle memory well and including a “supervisor” boss-like component, researchers got Claude Opus 5 to achieve a 100% score on the interactive reasoning benchmark ARC-AGI-3 — a set of 2D games with no instructions, where the model has to figure out how to play and win, similar to how a human would. (That’s a benchmark that has particularly irked rival frontier lab OpenAI.) Without the harness, Opus 5 scored 30%, which was the top result among all the models tested. Nvidia’s research is another indicator that, while model choice does matter, the model itself — the part that acts as the agent’s “brain” — is a smaller part of an agentic system than many AI users realize, especially for long-horizon tasks. The harness is what makes a model an agent: It handles memory, context, and feedback. “Generally speaking, the world interprets an agent almost as an API of the model,” Adel El Hallak, vice president of product in Nvidia’s AI unit (pictured above), tells TechCrunch. items.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital data centers as launch options dry up
items.description: There's about to be a big fight to secure access to space.
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: Starcloud , a startup developing satellites that can perform AI inference in orbit, told TechCrunch that it has added a $250 million extension to its March $170 million Series A funding round. The extension values the company at $2.3 billion. The additional capital will allow the company to open a larger manufacturing facility and advance its largest orbital data center spacecraft, Starcloud-3, which is intended to fly on SpaceX’s forthcoming Starship rocket. CEO Philip Johnston is also amassing capital to ensure that he can launch his satellites as the market for rocket transportation tightens up. “We can see what’s coming — we’re going to need to book an enormous amount of launch,” Johnston told TechCrunch. Starcloud has already requested permission from the FCC to operate 88,000 spacecraft. “As soon as we can, we want to get under contract with things like Starship,” Johnston said. “One of the biggest costs is now on securing your launch capacity…launch is pretty constrained right now because [SpaceX’s] Falcon 9 program is scheduled to end in 2028.” Launch costs were already one of the biggest challenges for orbital data center startups, to the point that one startup has decided to build its own rockets. SpaceX is now planning to phase out its workhorse vehicle and bring the much larger, but still unproven, Starship rocket online, making planning more difficult for satellite operators. items.title: Humanoids beat Usain Bolt’s 100m record
items.description: PLUS: Waymo builds a robotaxi brain
items.content: Good morning, robotics enthusiasts. At Beijing’s World Humanoid Robot Games, Tiangong Ultra tore through the 100 meters in 9.39 seconds — faster than Usain Bolt’s 9.58s world record. Honor’s Lightning came in second at 9.47s, also faster than the human world record. Anything with a motor was always going to smoke us in a footrace. But these robots are improving fast: this year’s 100m times are 2.3× faster than last year’s winning pace. The Rundown: A Chinese humanoid ran 100 meters in 9.39 seconds at Beijing's World Humanoid Robot Games — faster than Usain Bolt's world record — then slammed into the deceleration mat and stumbled into the sidelines. Tiangong Ultra clocked 9.39s, per state broadcaster CCTV, inside Bolt's 9.58s from Berlin 2009; Honor's Lightning took second at 9.47s. The same model beat the human 400m record by nearly five seconds, running 38.15s against Wayde van Niekerk's 43.03s from Rio 2016. Not everything cleared the bar. Runners failed to start or collapsed at the gun; a boxer folded over the ropes and stayed there until humans hauled it out.

items.title: A mystery challenger at the AI frontier
items.description: PLUS: Use Gemini Canvas to visualize Google Sheets
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to the 11,000 new readers who joined this weekend. A new, seemingly capable AI has landed on the block, and no one knows who built it. The weekend has been all about "Ox Alpha," which showed up on OpenRouter with no lab name attached, frontier-level coding scores, and free access — leaving developers to play detective over its origins. The Rundown: An anonymous model, Ox Alpha, just launched for free on OpenRouter — with 1M-token context and multimodal input, built for coding, sustained agentic work, and production workloads — and sent the internet scrambling to ID its maker. Ox Alpha made headlines Friday after hitting 80% on a DeepSWE subset, but full testing put it at 63%, near Fable 5 at far fewer tokens per task. Early forensics, including the AI’s answers and Chinese zodiac-based naming, suggest it’s from China’s Zhipu AI, potentially GLM-5.3 Flash or GLM-6 . Another potential candidate is Microsoft’s MAI family, though all four anonymous drops on OpenRouter in six months have been from Chinese labs.

items.title: The mRNA cancer vaccine finally delivers
items.description: PLUS: Spirit Airlines' data turns into bidding war
items.content: Good morning, tech enthusiasts. After decades of false starts, the mRNA cancer vaccine may have found its moment — Moderna and Merck’s personalized shot is the first mRNA cancer therapy to beat an active standard of care in Phase 3. It’s early evidence that the pandemic’s breakout technology can be aimed at the mutations inside one patient’s tumor, and melanoma is just the start. Image source: Julio C. Valencia at the NCI Center for Cancer Research (melanoma) The Rundown: Moderna and Merck’s made-to-order mRNA cancer vaccine has cleared its biggest test yet, beating Keytruda alone in a Phase 3 melanoma trial — the first late-stage win for an mRNA cancer therapy. The trial had 1,137 patients whose stage IIB–IV melanoma had been removed, randomizing them 2:1 to Moderna’s vaccine plus Keytruda or Keytruda alone. The vaccine — Intismeran Autogene — is manufactured for one person only; doctors sequence the tumor, then encode up to 34 of its mutations into mRNA.

items.content: Good morning, robotics enthusiasts. Unitree just became a $50B robotics company after a 460% IPO surge made founder Wang Xingxing ~$13B richer in a single day. It’s the first pure-play humanoid maker to list in mainland China, and retail investors bid more than 8K times the shares on offer. items.title: Pacing comes to the AI frontier
items.description: PLUS: Build, test, and publish an app without leaving Codex
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to the 5,705 new readers who joined us yesterday. Last month, over a thousand frontier AI staffers asked the industry for an option to slow down. OpenAI just showed what that looks like in practice, though two weeks might not have been what they had in mind. The company revealed a (now-finished) pause on training its upcoming models, with its largest planned run now “on hold” for further safety testing. Whether the “pacing” lasts may depend on the next security breach or the competition. The Rundown: OpenAI just confirmed it paused training on its future models for two weeks and is “pacing” development of its biggest frontier run, with Sam Altman telling reporter Alex Heath that private models are showing "various degrees of misalignment." The move follows July's breach that hacked Hugging Face, where OAI agents escaped a sandbox and reportedly coordinated on a message board for weeks. An Aug. 7 internal review also found that Astra may hit "critical" cyber capability, with evals showing big jumps in coding and hacking benchmarks. Automated investigators will now review model actions and reasoning, with staff meant to halt work unless they dismiss an alert as false within 30 minutes.

items.title: The $1.4T case against Meta
items.description: First glimpse of Apple's camera-embedded AirPods
items.content: Good morning, tech enthusiasts. Meta goes to trial in Oakland today, with four states arguing it knew Instagram and Facebook could hurt kids but built them to keep kids scrolling anyway. It’s the biggest test yet of an accusation parents, lawmakers, and whistleblowers have made for years — this time in a federal courtroom, with Mark Zuckerberg on the witness list and Instagram’s core mechanics on the table. The Rundown: Meta heads into its biggest youth-safety trial yet, with dozens of states accusing it of illegally harvesting children’s data and designing Facebook and Instagram to hook young users, with penalties Meta pegs at $1.4T. California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey are taking Meta to trial over claims that it misled consumers about the risks of its platforms. The $1.4T (roughly Meta’s entire market value) came from Meta, not the states; California’s lawyer told the court last week that $193B is the closer figure. The remedies reach into product mechanics: age gates, no infinite scroll or push notifications, deletion of every model trained on kids’ data, etc.

items.title: Cursor's Origin hits GitHub on its worst day
items.description: PLUS: How to set up ChatGPT to write in your voice
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 5,482 new readers. If you were picking a day to launch a GitHub competitor, you couldn't script a better one than the morning the legacy platform suffered a massive outage. Cursor just managed to hit that window, launching Origin as an alternative to the place the world has held its code for two decades. Microsoft is no stranger to defending from AI challengers, but one of its most entrenched products just joined the list. The Rundown: SpaceXAI’s coding platform Cursor just launched Origin, an early beta that hosts code repos and pull requests with agents built in, moving the company onto GitHub's turf the same day it suffered a massive outage for a large chunk of the day. The platform pairs each hosted repository with Cursor’s agent and review tool, keeping code browsing, follow-up edits, and human approval in one product. Users can sync their connected codebases right from GitHub, creating a live mirrored version that pushes to both platforms to test drive the new alternative. GitHub’s outage was its second major issue this month, with some functionality seeing performance issues for over 6 hours.

items.title: Robot vacuums finally learn gestures
items.description: PLUS: Robots build a Colorado neighborhood
items.content: Good morning, robotics enthusiasts. Washington has effectively blocked new foreign-made robot vacuums, squeezing the Chinese brands that own the category — and California-built Matic picked a good moment to give its vacuum bot a genuinely new trick. A free update lets you talk to the machine directly, pointing to a mess and telling it to “clean this.” The Chinese rivals still have more elaborate hardware, but Matic may have found the more interesting interface. The Rundown: Matic, a Silicon Valley robot-vacuum startup, is turning on voice controls that let owners point at a spill and tell the $1,245 floor bot to clean it — an attempt to differentiate in a market dominated by Chinese hardware rivals. Matic Cues lets you say “clean the kitchen” or point at a spill and say “clean this,” combining voice with five cameras to locate targets in 3D. It understands 70+ languages, with commands sent straight to the robot; voice recognition is powered by Google Gemini. The free OTA update uses hardware already onboard. In 9to5Mac’s test , voice was quick and reliable; pointing worked, but more slowly.
